title: Wheels to Meals: Measuring the Impact of Micromobility on Restaurant Demand
near_miss_reason: Assignment-unit-specific linear trends (city-specific linear time trends theta_c * t) in every reported column (Equation 1; Tables 2-6); Table 2 and Table 3 columns 1-3 are additionally estimated with CEM or PSM matching weights (matching-based DiD), while Table 3 columns 4-6 (unmatched) violate only the unit-trend rule. Staggered binary e-scooter entry at city-specific dates (June-October 2018, 49 treated cities), individual and week FE, never-treated control cities. Earnest card-panel data are proprietary and not shipped.
eligible_reason: The design qualifies (binary e-scooter entry switching on at city-specific dates between June and October 2018 for 49 treated cities, 49 never-treated matched control cities, individual and week FE), but no main-text specification satisfies the protocol. Every estimate is from Equation 1, which includes city-specific linear time trends theta_c * t; the protocol excludes unit-specific (here assignment-unit-specific) trends. The preferred specification (Table 2) and Table 3 columns 1-3 are additionally estimated on coarsened-exact-matched or propensity-score-matched samples (matching-based DiD). Table 3 columns 4-6 are unmatched but still include the city trends. No trend-free TWFE or event-study path is reported in the main text (Web Appendix H re-estimates trends on pretreatment data only, still a trend specification).
design_notes: Equation 1: log(Spend_it + 1) = b0 + b1*ScooterEntry_c(i)t + phi_i (individual FE) + xi_t (week FE) + theta_c*t (city-specific linear trend) + e_it. Earnest Analytics credit/debit card panel, 46,451 individuals in 98 cities, weekly, Jan 2017-Feb 2020. Treated individuals = e-scooter users in treated cities; controls from matched cities. CEM (preferred), PSM and unmatched samples; SEs clustered by city. Figure 3 and Equation 2 give a pretrend check (linear trend difference). Robustness: IHS outcome (Table 4), placebo categories (Table 6), permutation test, quadratic trends and pre-period-estimated trends (Web Appendix G-H), daily/monthly/five-month time units (Web Appendix G). Goodman-Bacon (2021) cited to motivate trends and the collapsed-time robustness check.

data_availability_statement: No availability statement found. Individual-level credit and debit card panel from Earnest Analytics (acknowledged for 'providing access'); city e-scooter entry dates compiled by the authors (Web Appendix B).
screener_notes: Design-level the paper is a textbook staggered DiD with never-treated controls (54 cities entered June-Oct 2018, 5 dropped by matching; 15 earlier and 29 later entrants excluded). The only barrier is the city-specific linear trend in every reported column (plus CEM/PSM weights in the preferred columns). If the lead decides that assignment-unit linear trends are tolerable, Table 3 columns 4-6 (unmatched) would be the cleanest candidates; I excluded them following the protocol's unit-specific-trends rule. Exact adoption dates by city are in Web Appendix B, not in the main text, so the number of weekly cohorts is unknown.
hand_check_nov4: Near-miss (unit trends; matching weights). Record coded under the earlier rule (eligible_design true, n_eligible_specs 0) and never entered near_miss.csv; every main-text column carries city-specific linear trends per the record's spec list and Equation 1, so the staggered binary design fails only on restrictions. Not controls-only.
